content.title: The Cognitive Shift: From Arithmetic to Algebra
content.text: Algebra is the "gatekeeper" subject. To pass the gate, you must stop calculating answers and start understanding relationships.

content.html:
What does "=" actually mean?

Arithmetic (Elementary School)

2 + 3 = ?

Here, the sign means "Do the math and write the answer." It is an action.

Algebra (Middle School)

3x + 4 = 5x - 6

Here, the sign means "These two things are balanced." It is a relationship.

videos.analysis:
Review: Sal Khan’s approach is foundational. He avoids starting with numbers, instead using a visual balance scale animation where he physically removes 'weights'.

Why it works: It anchors the 'Subtraction Property of Equality' in physical intuition, preventing the student from viewing algebra as a set of arbitrary rules.

videos.analysis:
Review: Mr. J acts as a drill sergeant for procedure. His bold handwriting and color-coding (red for inverse operations) reduce visual clutter.

Why it works: According to Cognitive Load Theory, this clean presentation helps novices focus entirely on the algorithm: Move Variables → Move Constants → Divide.

content.html:
Study Guide

The Algebraic Foundation

1 The Balance Scale (Variables on Both Sides)

"Algebra is a game of fairness. If you change one side, you must change the other."

Step-by-Step Recipe

  1. Identify Variables: Find terms with letters ($3x$, $5x$).
  2. Move Smallest: Subtract the smaller variable term from both sides.
  3. Isolate: Move the constant numbers away from the variable.
  4. Divide: Divide by the coefficient to find $x$.

2 Literal Equations (Solving for y)

"Think of it as furniture rearrangement. You don't throw the sofa out, you just move it to the other wall."

The "Undo" Method

Goal:Get $y$ alone on the left side ($y = ...$)
The Catch:You cannot combine unlike terms. $5 - 2x$ is NOT $3x$.
Tip:Use the Heart Method when dividing. Divide every single term individually.
Print this guide for your notebook.

quiz_data.q: Solve for x: 5x - 3 = 3x + 7
quiz_data.analysis:
Problem A1 Analysis

Cognitive Check: Variables are on both sides. Apply 'Move Smallest'.

  • Compare $5x$ and $3x$. Subtract $3x$ from both sides ($2x - 3 = 7$).
  • Add 3 to both sides ($2x = 10$).
  • Divide by 2 ($x = 5$).

quiz_data.q: Solve for k: 12 - 2k = 3k + 2
quiz_data.analysis:
Problem A2 Analysis

Trap Warning: Negative coefficients.

  • Comparing $-2k$ and $3k$, $-2k$ is smaller. Add $2k$ to both sides.
  • $12 = 5k + 2$.
  • Subtract 2: $10 = 5k$. Divide by 5: $k = 2$.

quiz_data.q: Rewrite in Slope-Intercept Form: 4x + 2y = 12
quiz_data.analysis:
Problem B1 Analysis

  • Subtract $4x$: $2y = -4x + 12$.
  • Divide everything by 2: $y = -2x + 6$.
  • Slope is -2, Intercept is 6.

quiz_data.q: Rewrite in Slope-Intercept Form: 3x - 4y = 8
quiz_data.analysis:
Problem B2 Analysis

Attention: The negative sign stays with the y.

  • Subtract $3x$: $-4y = -3x + 8$.
  • Divide by -4. Note: -3-4 becomes positive 34.
  • $8 / -4 = -2$. Final: $y = 34x - 2$.

content.title: System Types
content.content:
• One Solution (Intersect)

    Different slopes ($m$). They cross at one $(x,y)$.

  • No Solution (Parallel)

    Same slope ($m$), different start ($b$). Never touch.

  • Infinite (Same Line)

    Same slope ($m$), same start ($b$). It's the same line.

content.title: Substitution
content.content:
Ex: $y = \color{red}2x$ and $x + y = 12$

  1. Plug In: Put $(\color{red}2x)$ into $y$ in eq 2.
    $\rightarrow x + (2x) = 12$
  2. Solve: $3x = 12 \rightarrow \mathbf{x = 4}$
  3. Finish: Plug $x$ back to find $y$.
    $\rightarrow y = 2(4) = 8$. Ans: $(4, 8)$

content.title: Elimination
content.content:
Ex: $2x + y = 10$ and $2x - y = 2$

  1. Stack & Add: Add equations vertically.
    $\rightarrow (2x+2x) + (y-y) = 12 \rightarrow 4x = 12$
  2. Solve: $\mathbf{x = 3}$
  3. Finish: Plug $x$ back to find $y$.
    $\rightarrow 2(3) + y = 10 \rightarrow y=4$

content.title: Shading Strategy
content.content:
• 1Is y alone?
    $y >$ shade UP (sky)
    $y <$ shade DOWN (ground).
  • 2Test Point (0,0): Plug in $(0,0)$.
    True statement ($0 < 10$)? Shade $(0,0)$ side.
    False statement? Shade other side.
  • !Flip Warning: If you multiply or divide by a NEGATIVE number, FLIP the sign!

cards.title: The 'Flip' Rule
cards.text: When you multiply or divide by a negative number, you MUST flip the inequality symbol ($<$ becomes $>$).

cards.title: Check Your Work
cards.text: Found $(x,y)$? Plug it back into BOTH original equations. It must work for both!

cards.title: The 'Disappearing Var'
cards.text: If variables cancel out and you get $5=5$, it's Infinite Solutions. If you get $0=5$, it's No Solution.

cards.title: Slope Sanity Check
cards.text: Going UP from left-to-right? Slope must be (+). Going DOWN? Slope must be (-).

content.title: Mastering the Line
content.text: Now that you can move the numbers (Algebra), it's time to visualize them (Geometry). You are about to learn that every equation tells a story about a line.

content:
The "GPS" of Algebra

The equation y = mx + b is just a set of directions.

  • • b tells you where to Start.
  • • m tells you how to Move.

Line Relationships

Once you know the "Move" (slope), you can create new lines that run parallel (like train tracks) or smash through at 90 degrees (perpendicular).

content.html:
Cheat Sheet

Phase 2: Mastering the Line

1. Graphing $y = mx + b$

b = BEGIN (Y-Intercept)

Always graph this first! Put a dot on the Y-axis (the vertical line) at this number.

m = MOVE (Slope)

From your beginning dot, count the Rise/Run.

  • Top number: Up (+) or Down (-)
  • Bottom number: Always Right

2. Slope Relationships

TypeRuleExample
ParallelSame Slope ($m_1 = m_2$)$2/3 \rightarrow 2/3$
PerpendicularNegative Reciprocal ("Flip & Switch")$2/3 \rightarrow -3/2$

quiz_data.q: In the equation y = 3x - 2, where do you start graphing?
quiz_data.expl: The b value (-2) is the Begin point on the Y-axis.

quiz_data.q: What does a slope of 23 mean?
quiz_data.expl: Slope is Rise over Run. Top number (2) is Rise (Up), bottom (3) is Run (Right).

quiz_data.q: Which slope is parallel to m = 4?
quiz_data.expl: Parallel lines have the exact same slope.

quiz_data.q: Which slope is perpendicular to 25?
quiz_data.expl: Perpendicular slopes are Negative Reciprocals. Flip 2/5 to 5/2, then switch sign to negative.

quiz_data.question: What is the slope of any line parallel to the line y = 4x - 7?

options.feedback: Correct! Parallel lines always have identical slopes.
Careful. That would be a reflection, not parallel.
That's the reciprocal. We want the EXACT same slope.
That would be perpendicular (negative reciprocal).

quiz_data.question: Which equation represents a VERTICAL line passing through (-2, 5)?

options.feedback: y = number is always horizontal (floor/ceiling).
Correct! Vertical lines are always x = something.
This is horizontal because it starts with y =.
Check the point again. The x-coordinate is -2.

quiz_data.question: Choose the correct Point-Slope equation for slope -3 passing through (2, -1).

options.feedback: Watch your signs! The formula has minus signs built in.
Perfect. y - (-1) becomes y + 1.
You swapped x and y!
That's slope-intercept form, not point-slope.

quiz_data.question: If two lines intersect at point (-1, 3), what is the solution to the system?

options.feedback: They intersect, so there IS a solution.
Yes! The intersection point IS the solution.
Careful, you swapped x and y.
That only happens if the lines are identical.

quiz_data.question: Find the equation of a line parallel to y = ½x + 3 passing through (4, 0).

options.feedback: Correct! Same slope (½), different intercept.
You flipped the slope. Parallel means SAME slope.
That's perpendicular.
Check your math for 'b' again.

quiz_data.question: What is the slope of the line x = 8?

options.feedback: 0 slope is flat (horizontal). This line is vertical.
8 is just the location, not the steepness.
Correct! Vertical lines have undefined slope (division by zero).
Slope of 1 is a diagonal line.

quiz_data.question: What is the slope of the line y = -3?

options.feedback: Correct! It's a flat horizontal line.
-3 is the y-intercept, not the slope.
Undefined is for vertical lines.
Slope 1 is diagonal.

quiz_data.question: How many solutions for the system: y = 2x and y = 2x + 1?

options.feedback: Correct! Same slope (2) means they are parallel and never touch.
Do they have different slopes? No.
Lines can never intersect exactly twice.
Are they the same line? No, different y-intercepts.

quiz_data.question: Which equation is a horizontal line through (0, 5)?

options.feedback: Yes! Horizontal is y = number.
x = 5 is vertical.
That's a diagonal line with slope 5.
That's the y-axis (vertical).

quiz_data.question: In y - y1 = m(x - x1), what is 'm'?

options.feedback: Always! m is for Move/Slope.
b is usually y-intercept.
x1 is the x-coordinate.
y1 is the y-coordinate.

content.title: Where Lines Collide
content.text: You mastered drawing one line. Now we put two lines on the graph and ask: "Where do they meet?" This is the heart of Systems of Equations.

content:
1. The Intersection

The "Solution" is just the coordinate point $(x, y)$ where two lines cross paths.

2. The Tools

Sometimes graphing is messy. We use algebra tools (Substitution & Elimination) to get exact answers.

3. The Shading

Finally, we handle Inequalities ($<$ or $>$). These aren't just lines; they are whole regions of answers.

content.title: Visual Systems
content.subtitle: Adjust the sliders. The answer is the purple dot.

content:
Substitution ("The Spy")

Best when one variable is already alone (isolated).

Eq A: y = 2x + 1
Eq B: 3x + y = 11
Step 1: The Switch
Take 2x+1 and plug it into y in the second equation.
3x + (2x + 1) = 11
Step 2: Solve X
5x + 1 = 11
5x = 10
x = 2

Elimination ("The Combo")

Best when variables are stacked up nicely (Standard Form).

  2x + 3y = 20
-2x + y  = 4
----------------
Step 1: Add Down
The 2x and -2x cancel out (eliminate) to zero!
0 + 4y = 24
Step 2: Solve Y
4y = 24
y = 6

content.question: Which method is best for: y = 3x - 1 and y = -2x + 4?

options.feedback: Correct! Since both equal y, you can just set them equal to each other (Substitution).
Not quite. Elimination is best when variables are on the same side, like 2x + 3y = 10.

items.title: Graphing or Equaling
items.desc: Since both equal "y", set them equal to each other: $3x+2 = -5x-4$.

items.title: Substitution
items.desc: First equation tells you exactly what "y" is. Plug it into the second.

items.title: Elimination
items.desc: Look at -2y and +2y. If you add the lines, "y" dies immediately. Easy win.

quiz_data.q: If two lines have different slopes, how many times do they intersect?
quiz_data.expl: Different slopes mean they are angling towards each other and must cross eventually.

quiz_data.q:
Which method is best for:
$y = 2x + 1$
$3x + y = 10$
quiz_data.expl: Since the first equation has 'y' isolated, Substitution is the easiest path.

quiz_data.q: In the inequality $y < 2x - 1$, should the line be solid or dashed?
quiz_data.expl: Because it is strictly less than (<) and NOT equal to, the boundary is Dashed.

quiz_data.q: If you end up with $5 = 5$ when solving algebraically, what does it mean?
quiz_data.expl: A true statement (5=5) means the lines are actually identical (coincident lines).

quiz_data.question: What does the solution to a system of equations look like on a graph?

options.text: Two parallel lines that never touch
options.feedback: That would be 'No Solution'.

options.text: The point where the two lines intersect (cross)
options.feedback: Correct! The crossing point is the answer.

options.text: The y-intercept of the first line
options.feedback: That's just where the line starts.

quiz_data.question: In the equation y = -2/5x - 1, how do you move to find the next point?

options.feedback: Negative slope means go DOWN.
Yes. Negative top number = Down. Bottom number = Right.
Going Down AND Left makes a positive line (double negative).

quiz_data.question: If a point is the solution, what happens if you plug it into BOTH equations?

options.text: It works for both equations (makes them true)
options.feedback: Exactly. It is the only point that works for everyone.

options.text: It only works for the first equation
options.feedback: Then it's just a point on one line, not the system solution.
Not necessarily.

quiz_data.question: For the problem we just solved, what was the coordinate of the solution?

options.feedback: Close, but check the x-axis sign.
Perfect. Left 5, Up 1.
That was the intercept of the first line.
